carmen: Heads up — onboarding of nebula-m7 (HF safetensors) shows ~30% perf regression vs our expected profile. Profiler points to a kernel fallback to generic matmul for attention. Logs + numbers below.

aj: Can you paste the raw parse logs and the model config we ended up with? Missing metadata fields (num_attention_heads / head_dim) tend to trigger fallbacks.

carmen: Paste from the canary run: 
```\n[2026-03-15T10:12:03Z] parse: safetensors metadata keys: ['dtype','shape'] (missing num_attention_heads, attn_head_size, rope_scaling)\n[2026-03-15T10:12:04Z] runtime: kernel_selector -> generic_matmul (fallback)\n[2026-03-15T10:12:05Z] perf: p50 token latency = 12.3ms (baseline 8.5ms)\n[2026-03-15T10:12:05Z] perf: tokens/sec = 320 (baseline 450)\n[2026-03-15T10:12:05Z] trace: serve::kernel_selector::choose() -> generic_matmul\n```

devon: Hm. We've seen HF safetensors conversions that drop attn metadata when conversion script uses an old template. If head_dim can't be inferred, our parser intentionally punts which cascades to a conservative kernel choice. Also worth noting: RoPE scaling key mismatch can change the kernel path — if rope_scale isn't detected we avoid fused_rope kernels.

carmen: Indeed — the file had a metadata key named 'rotary_scaling' (legacy) instead of 'rope_scaling' so our parser skipped ropescale. That seems to have prevented the fused_rope_kv path.

aj: On the runtime side, kernel_selector currently prefers fused_rope_kv when (rope_scale present) AND (head_dim % 16 == 0). If rope_scale missing we pick generic_matmul. We should add a conservative heuristic: if head_dim aligns and tensors match expected shapes, attempt fused kernel and run quick validation.

samir: I'll take two parallel fixes: 1) backfill missing safetensors keys in the hf-conversion script (best-effort inference); 2) runtime change to probe optimized kernels when heuristics look OK, with a deterministic correctness check. I'll open PRs and run canary.

ml-onboard-bot: Canary deploy started: infra/canary/nebula-m7-2165001234 (will report status)

devon: Quick conversion snippet I'd apply in hf-convert: 
```python\n# best-effort backfill\nif 'num_attention_heads' not in cfg and 'hidden_size' in cfg:\n    # fallback defaults: try common head counts then compute head size\n    for try_heads in (32, 16, 8):\n        if cfg['hidden_size'] % try_heads == 0:\n            cfg['num_attention_heads'] = try_heads\n            cfg['attn_head_size'] = cfg['hidden_size'] // try_heads\n            break\n```

aj: That pattern is fine. Avoid hardcoding single default; try factors. Also check for attn_head_size / head_dim keys used by different HF families.

carmen: I applied the runtime kernel probe locally (try fused_rope_kv then validate small output checksum). Local perf after the tweak: tokens/sec 440, p50 8.9ms — close to baseline. Results pushed to issue #4827 with trace artifacts. :rocket:

samir: Thanks. I'm going to merge the conversion backfill PR and the runtime kernel_selector probe into the canary branch, run the perf-suite regression tests, then promote if green. I'll also add a targeted unit test that fails if optimized kernel is skipped when metadata is present.

devon: Also propose a UX change: onboard UI should warn when safetensors metadata is missing keys we care about (num_attention_heads, attn_head_size, rope_scaling). Saves debugging time.

carmen: Agreed. Filing follow-ups: ONBOARD-118 (UI warn), ONBOARD-119 (safetensors lint). Closing this triage — will update thread when canary is promoted.
